run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:45:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans: frontend-proxy's `ingress` spans fail with HTTP 504 after ~15.0s, and their rate rose from a baseline of ~0-0.03/s to ~0.18-0.34/s during 14:45-14:55. The 504s are a downstream symptom, not a proxy fault: a sampled trace shows load-generator POST (504, 15.097s) -> frontend-proxy ingress (504, 15.094s) -> frontend-proxy `router frontend egress` (15.061s) -> frontend `POST /api/checkout` (200, 18.232s) -> checkout `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` (17.510s) -> checkout `orders publish` (17.438s). The proxy aborts at ~15s while the frontend keeps working and answers 200 at ~18s. Checkout's Kafka producer is the source of the slowdown: checkout app logs show `orders publish` completing in 131-343µs at 14:41:48-14:41:58 but taking 11.45-26.09s at 14:48-14:52, and the share of checkout `orders publish` spans over 10s went from 0% (all points 14:25-14:45) to 91.6% at 14:50 and 96.1% at 14:55. This coincides with a kafka Deployment rollout: ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 (revision 2) was created at 14:42:37, the old kafka-ff7884766 pod was deleted at 14:42:39, checkout hit `connect: connection refused` to kafka:9092 from 14:43:32 to 14:44:09 with `circuit breaker is open`, the new broker only started listening on 9092 at 14:44:14, and the `orders-0` partition log was created fresh at 14:44:18 with initial high watermark 0 (broker data on /tmp/kafka-logs was lost). Kafka CPU throttling peaked at 0.403 of CFS periods around 14:45 but was back to ~0.01 by 14:49, while produce latency stayed at 11-26s, so throttling alone does not explain the sustained latency; the broker-side mechanism is not observable in the available metrics. Checked and not supporting the alert: frontend has no error spans, frontend-proxy pod is running/ready with 0 restarts and serves non-checkout requests with fast 200s, and other checkout dependencies show no error-rate signal in the returned series.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error spans exist and are concentrated on span_name `ingress`: at 14:50 the 5m error rate was 0.267/s (status STATUS_CODE_ERROR) against 17.04/s UNSET, and the 15m increase at 14:50 was 102.4 error spans on `ingress` (0 on `router frontend egress`).
frontend-proxy ingress error rate (2m rate) was 0-0.033/s from 14:21 through 14:45, then jumped to 0.200/s at 14:46 and stayed at 0.178-0.300/s through 14:55.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans on operation `ingress` carry status tags {error:true, http.status_code:"504", otel.status_code:"ERROR"} with durations of 14,999,447-15,094,393 µs, i.e. the proxy fails requests at a ~15s boundary.

In trace e1149d121221112b45608659f572e755 the visible parent chain is: load-generator `POST` 15.097s with http.status_code 504 -> frontend-proxy `ingress` 15.094s with 504 -> frontend-proxy `router frontend egress` 15.061s -> frontend `POST /api/checkout` 18.232s with http.status_code 200 -> frontend `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` -> checkout `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` 17.510s -> checkout `orders publish` 17.438s (producer span).
Checkout `orders publish` latency shifted abruptly: the fraction of those spans longer than 10s was 0 at every 5-minute point from 14:25 to 14:45, then 0.916 at 14:50 and 0.961 at 14:55.

Comparable baseline vs incident (>1s span fraction): checkout `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` 0.0066 at 14:30 -> 1.0 at 14:50; frontend `POST /api/checkout` 0.0265 -> 1.0; frontend-proxy `ingress` 0.0138 -> 0.0724.

checkout application logs confirm the producer slowdown: "Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 144.087µs / 131.794µs / 132.954µs ..." at 14:41:48-14:41:58, versus "Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 26.093517738s / 23.532669882s / 16.66880895s / 11.452121497s" at 14:48:39-14:52:18.

checkout produced hard Kafka failures between 14:43:32 and 14:44:09: "Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused", "client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to", "Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers", "Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open"; correspondingly checkout `orders publish` has error spans (15.94 error spans per 10m at 14:50, 0.147/s 2m rate at 14:46).

The kafka Deployment was rolled out at 14:42:37: ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 (deployment revision 2) was created 14:42:37 and the previous ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 (revision 1) now has 0 replicas; both have identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, identical env (KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS -Xmx400M -Xms400M etc.), no args and identical resources (limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi). Deployment kafka reports generation 2, 1 replica ready and available.

Namespace events show the controller replacing the kafka pod: "Scaled up replica set kafka-5c9d7cc485 from 0 to 1" at 14:42:37, SuccessfulCreate of pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 at 14:42:37, then Killing and SuccessfulDelete of pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 at 14:42:39.

The new kafka broker did not accept connections until 14:44:14: kafka logs show "Awaiting socket connections on 0.0.0.0:9092" and "[KafkaRaftServer nodeId=1] Kafka Server started" at 14:44:14.030; checkout reconnected with "Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (registered as #1)" at 14:44:22.

After the pod replacement the broker recreated the topic from scratch: "Sent auto-creation request for Set(orders)" and "Created log for partition orders-0 in /tmp/kafka-logs/orders-0", "[Partition orders-0 broker=1] Log loaded for partition orders-0 with initial high watermark 0", "Leader orders-0 ... starts at leader epoch 0 from offset 0" at 14:44:18.

The replacement kafka pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 (started 14:42:37, container started 14:42:38), and its working set was 588-622 MB against a 900Mi memory limit, so it is not memory-pressured.

Kafka CPU throttling spiked only around the restart: throttled-period ratio was 0.004-0.017 in the baseline, 0.403 at ~14:45 and 0.373 at ~14:47, then 0.0094-0.014 at 14:49-14:55; kafka CPU usage was 0.149 cores at ~14:45 and only 0.027 / 0.019 cores at ~14:50 / 14:55 while produce latency remained 11-26s.

frontend-proxy itself looks healthy: pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 is Running, ready, restartCount 0, started 14:09:34, and its access log at 14:52 shows fast 200 responses for non-checkout routes (e.g. `GET /api/cart` 24 ms, `GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ` 2 ms, `POST /api/cart` 221 ms).

frontend reported no error spans at all in the window: the only status series for frontend in the error-rate query is 0 for the full lookback, so the frontend failure mode here is latency only, not errors.

accounting `order-consumed` is not evidence of new impact: its >1s fraction was already 0.531 at the 14:30 baseline and 0.60 at 14:50, so an accounting regression should not be claimed from that figure.

A second, separate in-window change: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm has restartCount 2 and its last termination was reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 14:35:42Z, restarted 14:35:56Z; its error-rate series was 0 for the whole window.

The kafka Deployment update at 14:42:37 is the origin of the frontend-proxy alert: replacing the broker pod removed the Kafka endpoint (connection refused 14:43:32-14:44:09), forced checkout's producer circuit breaker open, destroyed the in-memory/ephemeral topic state (orders-0 recreated at 14:44:18 at offset 0), and afterwards checkout's produce calls succeeded but took 11-26s, driving checkout PlaceOrder to ~17-18s, which exceeded the frontend-proxy ~15s request limit and produced the 504s counted by the alert.

The sustained 11-26s produce latency after the broker was reachable (14:44:22 onward) is broker-side (log append/flush or request handling on the restarted, freshly-initialised broker); this is not verifiable here because Prometheus exposes no Kafka broker metrics for this target.

frontend-proxy is not failing because of an internal proxy fault or restart: its pod is running and ready with 0 restarts, non-checkout routes were served with 200s in milliseconds, and the failing `ingress` spans end at 504 after ~15s while the upstream frontend span in the same trace completes with 200 at 18.2s.

Kafka CPU throttling alone does not explain the prolonged slowdown: the throttled-period ratio returned to baseline (0.0094-0.014) by 14:49-14:55 while checkout produce durations were still 11.45-26.09s at 14:48-14:52 and 96.1% of `orders publish` spans still exceeded 10s at 14:55.

The fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 14:35:42 is not a plausible cause of this alert: it precedes the 14:43-14:46 onset of the frontend-proxy 504s, fraud-detection's error-rate series stayed 0, and it does not appear in the failing trace chain (checkout -> `orders publish`).

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so what changed in the kafka Deployment (generation 1 -> 2 at revision 2) and who/when changed it is unknown; only the resulting ReplicaSet differ (identical image/env/args/resources were compared, volumes, probes and other template fields were not compared, and the deleted kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 pod's logs are unavailable).

No Kafka broker metrics are present in Prometheus (a metric-name search for kafka/producer/messaging names returned nothing), so broker-side log-append, disk and request latency cannot be observed to prove why produces took 11-26s after 14:44:22.

Error-rate series were returned only for accounting, ad, checkout, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment and recommendation; cart, currency, email, shipping, product-catalog, quote and image-provider are unknown (not zero) for this window.
Trace evidence is a biased, incomplete sample (spans_omitted/incomplete set, error detail fields empty on sampled error spans), so the full call graph and exact error payloads are unknown.

frontend-proxy access logs hit the 4 MiB read limit at 14:45:08 and a filtered query for 504 lines over 14:55-14:57 returned no lines, so the access-log record of the 504 responses was not read end to end.
The impact of the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (exit 137, 14:35:42) on its own consumer function was not evaluated (its application logs were not read).
next_steps: Review the kafka Deployment's rollout history/annotations and any change record for the 14:42:37 update (revision 1 -> 2) to establish what was changed and why.
Inspect the restarted kafka broker's own metrics/logs (log-append time, request queue, disk I/O on node i-0caf4b73702b2641e) to explain the sustained 11-26s produce latency seen after 14:44:22.
Check whether the Kafka broker's log directory (/tmp/kafka-logs) is ephemeral and whether the topic data loss at 14:44:18 (orders-0 at high watermark 0) is expected for this deployment.

Compare frontend-proxy's route/request timeout (~15s, implied by 504s at ~15.0s) with the checkout path's observed ~18s latency, and consider whether the proxy timeout or checkout's Kafka produce path should be adjusted.
Follow up on the separate fraud-detection container OOMKill at 14:35:42 (exit 137) with its own logs and memory limit, independently of this alert.
